saints.name: St. John Baptist de la Salle
saints.title: Priest
saints.shortBlurb: A French canon who gave up rank and wealth to found free schools and train the teachers of the poor…
biography: Born at Reims in 1651, the son of a wealthy family, John Baptist de la Salle was made a cathedral canon at sixteen and ordained priest in 1678. His life turned in 1679 when he helped the schoolmaster Adrian Nyel open a school for poor boys; he went on to house the teachers in his home, resign his canonry, and sell his inheritance to feed the famine-stricken poor of Champagne.

With those schoolmasters he formed the Institute of the Brothers of the Christian Schools, the first religious institute with no priests among its members, bound to teach the poor gratuitously. He trained his masters in what is reckoned the first normal school, opened at Reims in 1685, and pioneered teaching in the vernacular, in classes rather than one by one.

Harassed by the schoolmasters' guilds and by churchmen opposed to a community of laymen teaching 'together and by association', he died at Saint-Yon near Rouen on Good Friday, 7 April 1719. Leo XIII canonized him in 1900; Pius XII declared him patron of all teachers of youth in 1950 — the founder of modern popular schooling made patron of those who continue it.
saints.knownFor: Founding the De La Salle Brothers and modern teacher training.
